definition_en: inside a place, container or period of time, or according to a rule
core_image: 一只手把东西完全放进盒子里，盒盖扣上
scene: 收拾房间时，最容易把东西一塞了事。The keys are still in the drawer.
sceneCN: 这里 in 是「在……里」（第 1 个义项：表示容器或空间的内部）；句意是钥匙还在抽屉里。

pos.zh: 介词：在……里；在……之内；按照
副词：进入；在内；在屋里

forms.label: 无变化（介词无词形变化）

derivatives.zh: 义为「在……之内」，是 in 与 with 合成的加强形式
义为「进入、到……里面」，动感强于 in
义为「在……里面」，与 in 近义但更强调内部

senses.title: Inside a container or space
senses.titleCN: 在……里：处于容器或空间内部
senses.definition: enclosed by or located inside a place or object
senses.definitionCN: 被某处或某物包围，处在它的内部
senses.example: The cat is asleep in the basket.
senses.exampleCN: 猫在篮子里睡着了。
senses.why: This is the oldest and most physical use: something is surrounded on every side.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老也最具体的用法：某物四面都被围住。

senses.title: Within a period of time
senses.titleCN: 在……之内：时间范围里
senses.definition: during a period, or before a limit of time ends
senses.definitionCN: 在某段时间之中，或在期限结束之前
senses.example: We will finish the report in two days.
senses.exampleCN: 我们会在两天之内完成报告。
senses.why: Time is pictured as a box too: what happens in it is held inside those hours.
senses.whyCN: 时间也被想成一个盒子：其中发生的事被这些小时「装」住。

senses.title: Using a language or a material
senses.titleCN: 用……：以某种语言或材料
senses.definition: by means of a language, medium, or material
senses.definitionCN: 借助某种语言、媒介或材料
senses.example: Please write your name in ink.
senses.exampleCN: 请用墨水写上你的名字。
senses.why: The medium surrounds the writing the way a container surrounds what it holds.
senses.whyCN: 媒介包围着字迹，就像容器包围着它所装的东西。

senses.title: According to a rule or state
senses.titleCN: 按照：符合规则或处于某种状态
senses.definition: showing the way something is arranged or a condition someone is in
senses.definitionCN: 表示某事的排列方式，或某人所处的状况
senses.example: The books are arranged in alphabetical order.
senses.exampleCN: 这些书按字母顺序排列。
senses.why: A pattern has an inside too: only what fits the arrangement counts as in it.
senses.whyCN: 模式也有「内部」：只有符合这个排列的东西才算在里头。

senses.title: Towards the inside, as an adverb
senses.titleCN: 进去：副词，朝里或在家
senses.definition: used after a verb to mean towards the inside, or at home
senses.definitionCN: 用在动词后，表示朝里面去，或表示在家
senses.example: Come in and shut the door.
senses.exampleCN: 进来把门关上。
senses.why: Once in frees itself from a noun, it becomes a small adverb of direction.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 in 摆脱了后面的名词，它就变成表示方向的小副词。

intro.en: In is one of the oldest words English has, from Old English in, a preposition of place shared by most Germanic languages.
intro.cn: in 是英语最古老的词之一，来自古英语 in，是多数日耳曼语言共有的方位介词。

items.en: The Germanic root meant both into and inside, with direction and place in one form.
items.cn: 日耳曼词根同时表示「进入」与「在里面」，方向与位置合于一体。

items.en: In worked with the dative case to say where something was.
items.cn: 古英语中 in 与与格连用，表示某物所在的位置。

items.en: Case endings faded, and in took over location on its own.
items.cn: 格词尾消失后，in 独自承担起表示位置的功能。

items.en: Fixed phrases such as in fact and in time turned the word into a part of idiom.
items.cn: in fact、in time 等固定说法让这个词成为习语的一部分。

items.en: The adverb use, as in come in, grew alongside the preposition.
items.cn: come in 这类副词用法与介词用法一同发展起来。

note.en: The look-alike group holds short function words built on the same frame; the near-meaning group holds prepositions of containment.
note.cn: 形近组收同一框架内的短虚词；近义组收表示「在内部」的介词。

entries.definition: Moving to a position inside something.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「进入」，含移动意味。

entries.definition: A small hotel that also serves food.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小旅馆」，与 in 同音。

entries.definition: Touching and supported by a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……上」，与 in 形近。

entries.definition: In the interior part of something.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……里面」，比 in 更强调内部。

entries.definition: Inside the limits of a place or time.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……范围内」，多用于抽象或时间。

entries.definition: Surrounded by several people or things.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……之中」，指处于群体之内。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the shape of the letters, the container image and the fixed phrases every learner meets first.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借字母形状、容器意象与学习者最先遇到的固定搭配。

normal.en: The letter i standing inside the frame of n looks like a thing dropped into a box.
normal.cn: 字母 i 立在 n 的框里，像东西落进盒子。

normal.en: In time and on time differ: in time means before the deadline, so the box is time itself.
normal.cn: in time 与 on time 不同：in time 是赶在期限之前，那只盒子就是时间。

normal.en: In English is a double in: the language is the container of the words.
normal.cn: in English 是两个 in：语言成了词语的容器。

normal.en: Come in is in without a noun, a bare direction pointing inward.
normal.cn: come in 是没有名词的 in，只是一个朝内的方向。

normal.en: In fact is a doorway phrase: the speaker steps from claim to evidence.
normal.cn: in fact 是一道门：说话人从论断走进证据。

abstract.en: A preposition is a map folded into one syllable: in draws the border of belonging.
abstract.cn: 介词是一张折进一个音节的地图：in 画出归属的边界。

abstract.en: To be in is to be held, and every membership is a soft wall around us.
abstract.cn: 身处其中就是被盛着，每一种归属都是围着我们的软墙。

abstract.en: Small words carry the heaviest grammar: in builds the rooms that nouns live in.
abstract.cn: 小词承担最重的语法：in 造出名词居住的房间。

examples.en: There is a small hole in the wall.
examples.cn: 墙上有一个小洞。

examples.en: She will be back in ten minutes.
examples.cn: 她十分钟后回来。

examples.en: Say it again in a louder voice.
examples.cn: 用更大的声音再说一遍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「印」——印章盖在纸上，墨就陷在纸里面。

root: 古英语 in，源自日耳曼语共同词根，与德语 in、荷兰语 in 同源；同族派生词有 into、within、inside。

sensesIntro.en: In begins as a word for being surrounded and spreads to time, medium, rule and finally to a bare adverb of inward motion.
sensesIntro.cn: in 起初表示「被围住」，而后铺展到时间、媒介、规则，最后成为表示朝内运动的副词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an object dropped inside a closed box.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件东西被放进合上的盒子。

branches.en: SPACE LINE: the thing is surrounded by walls.
branches.cn: 空间线：事物被四壁围住。

branches.en: TIME LINE: hours work as a box around events.
branches.cn: 时间线：小时成为包住事件的盒子。

branches.en: MEDIUM LINE: ink, voice or language wraps the content.
branches.cn: 媒介线：墨水、声音或语言包住内容。

branches.en: RULE LINE: only what fits the pattern is counted in.
branches.cn: 规则线：只有符合模式的东西才算在内。

branches.en: MOTION LINE: the word sheds its noun and points inward.
branches.cn: 运动线：这个词甩掉名词，指向内部。

intro.en: A Germanic preposition that also forms a family of compound words of place and time.
intro.cn: 一个日耳曼介词，同时构成一族表地点与时间的合成词。

latinIntro.en: Latin has its own in, meaning into or not, and English inherited many words built with it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语也有 in，表示「进入」或「不」，英语继承了大量由它构成的词。

definition_en: to have someone or something as a part of a larger group or whole
core_image: 敞开栅栏门，把站在外面的一个人也放进来
scene: 点名时总有人被漏掉，也总有人被补上。The price includes breakfast and one free drink.
sceneCN: 这里 include 是「包含」（第 1 个义项：整体之中含有一部分）；句意是价格里含早餐和一杯免费饮料。

pos.zh: 动词：包括；包含；计入

derivatives.zh: 由 include 加 -sion 构成，义为「包含、接纳」
义为「包含在内的、包容的」
义为「包括在内的」，常用于 tax included
义为「包括……在内」，作介词使用

senses.title: To contain as a part
senses.titleCN: 包含：作为整体的一部分
senses.definition: to have something as one of the parts of a whole
senses.definitionCN: 把某物作为整体的一部分而含有
senses.example: The price includes breakfast and one free drink.
senses.exampleCN: 价格包含早餐和一杯免费饮料。
senses.why: The Latin base claudere means to shut, and in-claudere shuts something inside the whole.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 claudere 意为「关闭」，in-claudere 就是把某物关进整体之内。

senses.title: To allow someone to join
senses.titleCN: 把……算进来：允许某人加入
senses.definition: to let a person become part of a group, list or activity
senses.definitionCN: 让某人成为群体、名单或活动的一部分
senses.example: Please include me in the next round of talks.
senses.exampleCN: 请把我也算进下一轮谈话。
senses.why: The fence image turns social: to include is to open the gate for a person standing outside.
senses.whyCN: 栅栏的意象转向人际：include 就是替站在外面的人打开门。

senses.title: To list something for attention
senses.titleCN: 列在文中：把某事写进内容
senses.definition: to mention a thing as part of a written list or set of details
senses.definitionCN: 作为书面清单或细节的一部分而提及
senses.example: The report includes three charts on rainfall.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告包含三张降雨图表。
senses.why: Writing is a container too: what is included is what the page holds.
senses.whyCN: 书写也是一种容器：被包含的东西就是页面所盛放的东西。

senses.title: Charged in addition to something
senses.titleCN: 另计在内：计费中的「含」
senses.definition: used on bills to show that a charge is already added
senses.definitionCN: 用于账单，表示某项费用已经加进去
senses.example: Service is included in the bill.
senses.exampleCN: 服务费已包含在账单里。
senses.why: Commercial use narrows the word to money: the sum already shuts the item in.
senses.whyCN: 商业用法把词收窄到金钱：总额已经把这一项关了进去。

intro.en: Include comes from Latin includere, to shut in, built from in, in, and claudere, to close.
intro.cn: include 来自拉丁语 includere「关在里面」，由 in「在内」与 claudere「关闭」构成。

items.en: Claudere meant to shut a door, and in-claudere meant to shut something inside.
items.cn: claudere 意为「关门」，in-claudere 则是「把某物关在里面」。

items.en: Classical writers used includere for enclosing a place or a list of names.
items.cn: 古典作家用 includere 表示围住一块地方或把名字列入其中。

items.en: Church and legal texts used it for items counted within a document.
items.cn: 教会与法律文本用它表示计入某文件之内的条目。

items.en: English took include for parts held inside a whole.
items.cn: 英语借 include 表示被整体所容纳的部分。

items.en: The social sense of admitting people grew in the last two centuries.
items.cn: 「接纳人」的社会义项在近两百年里发展起来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -clude shape; the near-meaning group holds verbs of holding something as part of a whole.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -clude 外形；近义组收表示「作为一部分含有」的动词。

entries.definition: To keep someone or something out on purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「排除、不让进入」，与 include 反义同根。

entries.definition: To finish or to reach a judgement.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「结束、得出结论」，与 include 同根。

entries.definition: The act of making someone part of a group.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「包含、接纳」。

entries.definition: To hold something inside.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「装有、包含」，更偏物理容纳。

entries.definition: To deal with or pay for something as well.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「涵盖、支付」，多用于范围与费用。

entries.definition: To make something a necessary part of an activity.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「涉及、需要含有」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the closed-door image, the ex-contrast and the everyday price tag.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借关门意象、ex- 对照与日常价签。

normal.en: In plus clude is in plus shut: include shuts the item inside the whole.
normal.cn: in 加 clude 就是「在内」加「关闭」：include 把条目关进整体里。

normal.en: Exclude has the same root with ex-, which means out, so the pair is gate open and gate shut.
normal.cn: exclude 同根但用 ex-「向外」，这一对就是开门与关门。

normal.en: Inclusive marks the price tag: what is included is already in the sum.
normal.cn: inclusive 写在价签上：被包含的已经算在总额里。

normal.en: Include me in is the social version of opening the fence.
normal.cn: include me in 就是「打开栅栏」的社交版本。

normal.en: A good report includes the awkward chart too, not only the handsome one.
normal.cn: 好的报告连那张不好看的图表也包含进去，而不只挑好看的。

abstract.en: To include is to decide that a boundary is wide enough for one more thing.
abstract.cn: 包含就是判定一道边界足够宽，还能再装下一件东西。

abstract.en: What a language includes shapes what its speakers can easily think.
abstract.cn: 一门语言包含什么，就塑造了说这门语言的人容易想到什么。

abstract.en: Whole and part only make sense together: include is the hinge between them.
abstract.cn: 整体与部分只有放在一起才有意义：include 就是两者的铰链。

examples.en: The tour includes two nights in a small hotel.
examples.cn: 这趟旅行包含在一家小旅馆住两晚。

examples.en: Her duties include answering the phone.
examples.cn: 她的职责包括接电话。

examples.en: Please include your student number on the form.
examples.cn: 请在表格上写上你的学号。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「印库路得」——把货物印进库房，就算包含入库里了。

root: 拉丁语 in（在内）+ claudere（关闭）→ includere（关在里面）；同根词有 exclude、conclude、preclude、inclusion、inclusive。

sensesIntro.en: Include shuts a thing inside a whole, and from that single image come containing parts, admitting people, listing details and charging sums.
sensesIntro.cn: include 把某物关进整体之中，仅凭这一意象就生出了含部分、接纳人、列细节与计费四路含义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fence gate opened long enough for one more person to step in.
core.cn: 核心意象：栅栏门敞开一会儿，让又一个人走进来。

branches.en: PART LINE: the whole holds the part inside.
branches.cn: 部分线：整体把部分容纳在内。

branches.en: PEOPLE LINE: someone outside is brought into the group.
branches.cn: 人的线：外面的人被带进群体里。

branches.en: PAGE LINE: a document holds the detail in print.
branches.cn: 页面线：文件用文字把细节收进去。

branches.en: MONEY LINE: the bill already shuts the charge in.
branches.cn: 金钱线：账单已经把这一项关了进去。

branches.en: ETHICS LINE: boundaries decide who is counted and who is not.
branches.cn: 伦理线：边界决定谁被算在内、谁不算。

intro.en: A Latin prefix for inside, a root for closing, and a family of words about boundaries.
intro.cn: 一个表「在内」的拉丁前缀、一个表「关闭」的词根，加一族与边界有关的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin in, in, and claudere, to shut, gave includere, to shut in.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 in「在内」与 claudere「关闭」合成 includere「关在里面」。

items.example: the root of exclude and include
items.exampleCN: exclude 与 include 的共同词根

items.meaning: the state of being shut in
items.example: the inclusion of a new member

items.exampleCN: 第十页到第二十页含首尾

definition_en: the money a person or business receives regularly from work or investments
core_image: 工资单上的数字顺着账本一栏流进来，落在月底的余额上
scene: 月底算账时，最先要看的是进账与支出。Her monthly income barely covers the rent.
sceneCN: 这里 income 是「收入」（第 1 个义项：定期得到的钱）；句意是她每月的收入勉强够付房租。

pos.zh: 名词：收入；收益；所得

derivatives.zh: 由 out 与 come 构成，义为「结果」，与 income 结构相对
义为「支出、开销」，与 income 相反
义为「工资、劳动所得」，是 income 的一种具体来源

senses.title: Money received from work
senses.titleCN: 收入：工作所得的进账
senses.definition: the money that comes in regularly from a job or business
senses.definitionCN: 由工作或经营定期进来的钱
senses.example: Her monthly income barely covers the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 她每月的收入勉强够付房租。
senses.why: The word is literally what comes in, so its first home is the household budget.
senses.whyCN: 这个词字面上就是「进来的东西」，所以它的第一个归宿是家庭账本。

senses.title: Money from investments
senses.titleCN: 收益：投资带来的进项
senses.definition: profit that arrives from savings, rent or shares rather than from labour
senses.definitionCN: 来自储蓄、房租或股票的收益，而非劳动所得
senses.example: Rent from the second flat is his only extra income.
senses.exampleCN: 第二套房子的租金是他唯一的额外收益。
senses.why: Any stream that flows in counts, whether it is paid by an employer or by an asset.
senses.whyCN: 凡是流进来的钱都算，无论付款方是雇主还是资产。

senses.title: A group's or country's revenue
senses.titleCN: 总收入：集体或国家的岁入
senses.definition: the total money that a company or a country takes in over a period
senses.definitionCN: 公司或国家在一段时间内的总进账
senses.example: Tourism provides a large share of the island's income.
senses.exampleCN: 旅游业提供了这座岛收入的一大部分。
senses.why: The same metaphor scales up: households, firms and nations all keep a ledger.
senses.whyCN: 同一个比喻可以放大：家庭、公司和国家的账本都是同样的记法。

senses.title: In economics, a flow of money
senses.titleCN: 所得：经济学中的流量概念
senses.definition: in economics, the flow of money received by a person or sector in a period
senses.definitionCN: 经济学中，个人或部门在一段时期内收到的货币流量
senses.example: Economists compare income with consumption rather than with wealth.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家把所得与消费比较，而不是与财富比较。
senses.why: The discipline needs a noun for a flow, and this compound supplies exactly that.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科需要一个指「流量」的名词，而这个合成词恰好提供。

intro.en: Income is a native English compound of in and come, first meaning simply what comes in.
intro.cn: income 是英语本土合成词，由 in 与 come 组成，最初只表示「进来的东西」。

items.en: Inncome and incuman described the act of coming in.
items.cn: inncome 与 incuman 描述「进来」这一动作。

items.en: The noun shifted from the act to the thing that arrives.
items.cn: 名词从「进来的动作」转指「到来的东西」。

items.en: By the seventeenth century income was used for revenue from land or trade.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，income 已用于指土地或贸易带来的收入。

items.en: Income tax made the word an everyday term in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 十九世纪的所得税让这个词成为日常用语。

items.en: Economics gave it a technical sense as a flow measured per period.
items.cn: 经济学又给了它「按时期计量流量」的专业含义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -come frame; the near-meaning group holds words for money received.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -come 框架；近义组收表示「收到的钱」的词。

entries.definition: The result that comes out of a process.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「结果」，与 income 结构相同。

entries.definition: A greeting given to a guest who comes.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「欢迎」，含 come 一词。

entries.definition: Arriving or about to arrive.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「进来的、即将到来的」。

entries.definition: A fixed payment made monthly or yearly.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「薪水」，指固定发放的报酬。

entries.definition: Money paid for work by the hour or day.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「工资」，多按小时或按天计。

entries.definition: Money a business or government takes in.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「营收、岁入」，更正式。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the literal come-in reading, the balanced ledger and the tax form.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借字面的「进来」含义、收支账本与税表。

normal.en: Income is simply what comes in, a two-word sentence packed into one noun.
normal.cn: income 就是「进来的东西」，把一个两词句压进一个名词。

normal.en: Outcome is the mirror: what comes out of a process is a result, not money.
normal.cn: outcome 是镜像：从过程里「出来」的是结果，不是钱。

normal.en: Income tax takes a slice of what has just come in.
normal.cn: income tax 是从刚进来的钱里切走一片。

normal.en: A steady income is a steady stream, which is why the money verbs are flow and run out.
normal.cn: steady income 是稳定的水流，所以谈钱会说 flow 或 run out。

normal.en: On a payslip the word sits at the top, above every deduction.
normal.cn: 在工资单上，这个词印在最上面，压在所有扣款之上。

abstract.en: Income measures a door that keeps opening, not a box that is already full.
abstract.cn: 收入衡量的是不断打开的门，而不是已经装满的箱子。

abstract.en: A budget is a story about which direction one prefers to face, inward or outward.
abstract.cn: 预算是一个关于你愿意朝哪边看的故事：向内还是向外。

abstract.en: To live on an income is to let a river decide the width of every bank.
abstract.cn: 靠一份收入生活，就是让一条河决定两岸的宽度。

examples.en: His income doubled after he changed jobs.
examples.cn: 换工作之后他的收入翻了一倍。

examples.en: The family lives on a fixed income.
examples.cn: 这家人靠固定收入生活。

examples.en: Low income often decides which school a child attends.
examples.cn: 低收入常常决定一个孩子上哪所学校。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「银卡姆」——银卡里的钱慢慢进来，就是收入。

root: 古英语 in「在内、进入」+ come「来」，字面义为「进来的东西」；对照 outcome、incoming。

sensesIntro.en: Income starts as a literal coming in, then widens from wages to investment returns, to a nation's revenue and to a technical flow.
sensesIntro.cn: income 起初只是字面的「进来」，后来从工资扩展到投资收益、国家岁入，再到专业上的流量概念。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a column of figures flowing in and settling at the month-end balance.
core.cn: 核心意象：一栏数字流进来，落在月底的余额上。

branches.en: WORK LINE: a job sends money in every month.
branches.cn: 工作线：每月由工作送来钱。

branches.en: ASSET LINE: rent and shares send money in without labour.
branches.cn: 资产线：房租与股票不需劳动就能送钱进来。

branches.en: SCALE LINE: firms and countries keep the same ledger.
branches.cn: 规模线：公司与国家用的是同一本账。

branches.en: THEORY LINE: economics measures the flow per period.
branches.cn: 理论线：经济学按时期计量这股流量。

branches.en: LEDGER LINE: income is always read against spending.
branches.cn: 账本线：收入永远要对着支出一起看。

intro.en: A Germanic preposition of coming in, joined with a Germanic verb, and a small family of -come words.
intro.cn: 一个表「进来」的日耳曼介词与一个日耳曼动词组合，形成一族以 -come 结尾的词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin equivalents are in and venire, which gave English words like revenue and invent.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的对应成分是 in 与 venire，英语由此得到 revenue、invent 等词。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 归还，由此得到「收益」之义

definition_en: to take something into a larger whole so that it becomes one part of it
core_image: 两块面团被揉在一起，再也分不清哪块是新的
scene: 改稿时常常把别人的建议揉进自己的段落里。The new plan incorporates ideas from every department.
sceneCN: 这里 incorporate 是「吸收合并」（第 2 个义项：把某物并进更大的整体）；句意是新计划吸收了各部门的想法。

pos.zh: 动词：包含；吸收；合并
形容词：合并的；一体化的（多用于法律文本）

derivatives.zh: 由 incorporate 加 -ion 构成，义为「合并、法人化」
义为「已合并的、组成法人的」，公司名后常缩写为 Inc.
义为「公司的、团体的」，与本词同根
义为「公司、法人团体」

senses.title: To contain as an integrated part
senses.titleCN: 包含：作为整体中的一部分
senses.definition: to include something so that it forms part of a whole
senses.definitionCN: 把某物纳入其中，使其成为整体的一部分
senses.example: The device incorporates a camera and a speaker.
senses.exampleCN: 这个设备里集成了摄像头和扬声器。
senses.why: The Latin corpus, body, supplies the image: something is given a body inside a larger body.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 corpus「身体」提供了意象：某物被放进更大的身体里，获得了一个位置。

senses.title: To absorb ideas or material
senses.titleCN: 吸收：把想法或材料并进来
senses.definition: to take in suggestions, methods or substances and make them one's own
senses.definitionCN: 把建议、方法或材料吸收进来变成自己的
senses.example: The new plan incorporates ideas from every department.
senses.exampleCN: 新计划吸收了各部门的想法。
senses.why: Dough is the natural picture: once kneaded, the added piece cannot be taken back out.
senses.whyCN: 面团是最自然的画面：一旦揉进去，加进来的那块就取不出来了。

senses.title: To combine into one body
senses.titleCN: 合并：把两个单位并成一个
senses.definition: to unite two organizations or territories into a single unit
senses.definitionCN: 把两个组织或地区并成一个单位
senses.example: The two villages were incorporated into one town.
senses.exampleCN: 两个村庄合并成了一个镇。
senses.why: Law extends the body image to groups: several bodies may become one body.
senses.whyCN: 法律把身体意象扩展到团体：几个身体合成一个身体。

senses.title: To form a legal company
senses.titleCN: 注册为法人：成立公司
senses.definition: to establish a business as a legal corporation
senses.definitionCN: 把一家企业设立为法律上的法人公司
senses.example: They incorporated the business last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 他们去年春天把这家企业注册成了公司。
senses.why: A company receives a legal body of its own, which is exactly what the root promises.
senses.whyCN: 公司获得了自己的法律身体，这正是词根所许诺的意思。

intro.en: Incorporate comes from Late Latin incorporare, to give a body to, from in and corpus, body.
intro.cn: incorporate 来自晚期拉丁语 incorporare「赋予身体」，由 in 与 corpus「身体」构成。

items.en: Corpus meant a body, and also a body of writing or of people.
items.cn: corpus 意为「身体」，也指一批文字或一群人。

items.en: Incorporare meant to unite things into one body.
items.cn: incorporare 意为把多个事物联合成一个身体。

items.en: English used incorporate for mixing substances and ideas into a whole.
items.cn: 英语用 incorporate 表示把材料与想法混入整体。

items.en: Legal use produced the sense of forming a corporation.
items.cn: 法律用法产生了「组成法人公司」的含义。

items.en: Modern business writing uses it for features built into a product.
items.cn: 现代商务写作又用它表示产品里内置的功能。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the corpor- body root; the near-meaning group holds verbs of joining things into one.
note.cn: 形近组共用表示「身体」的 corpor- 词根；近义组收表示「合为一体」的动词。

entries.definition: Relating to a large company.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「公司的、团体的」。

entries.definition: A company treated as one legal person.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「公司、法人团体」。

entries.definition: The act of uniting into one body.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「合并、法人化」。

entries.definition: To combine parts into a working whole.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「整合」，强调配合成完整系统。

entries.definition: To join two things so that they become one.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「合并」，多用于机构。

entries.definition: To take something in and make it part of oneself.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「吸收」，强调吞入并同化。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the body root, the kneaded dough and the company register.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借「身体」词根、揉面的动作与公司注册。

normal.en: In plus corporate: put a body inside a body, and the smaller one loses its outline.
normal.cn: in 加 corporate：把一个身体放进另一个身体，小的那个就失去了轮廓。

normal.en: Corpus is body, so corporation is a group given one legal body.
normal.cn: corpus 是身体，所以 corporation 就是被赋予一个法律身体的团体。

normal.en: Kneading dough is the best demonstration: after folding, no one can find the seam.
normal.cn: 揉面团是最好的演示：折过之后没人找得到接缝。

normal.en: Inc. after a company name is this word cut short.
normal.cn: 公司名后的 Inc. 就是这个词的缩写。

normal.en: A good editor incorporates the reader's question without letting it show.
normal.cn: 好编辑会把读者的疑问吸收进去，却不让人看出来。

abstract.en: To incorporate is to make difference disappear without erasing its contribution.
abstract.cn: 吸收就是让差异消失，却不清除它带来的贡献。

abstract.en: Every culture grows by incorporating what it first called foreign.
abstract.cn: 每种文化都靠吸收当初称为「外来」的东西而成长。

abstract.en: A whole is strong when it can still name the parts it has taken in.
abstract.cn: 一个整体之所以强，是因为它仍叫得出自己吸收过哪些部分。

examples.en: The recipe incorporates a little honey for sweetness.
examples.cn: 这个食谱加了一点蜂蜜来增甜。

examples.en: Teachers incorporate games into the first lesson.
examples.cn: 老师们把游戏融入第一堂课。

examples.en: The firm was incorporated in nineteen ninety.
examples.cn: 这家公司于一九九零年注册成立。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因科破瑞」——因为把学科破开重揉，就合并成了一门新学问。

root: 拉丁语 in（进入）+ corpus（身体）→ incorporare（赋予身体、合为一体）；同根词有 corporate、corporation、corpse、corps。

sensesIntro.en: Incorporate gives an incoming thing a body inside a larger body, so the word covers containing features, absorbing ideas, merging units and creating legal persons.
sensesIntro.cn: incorporate 让进来的东西在更大的身体里获得位置，因此涵盖内置功能、吸收想法、合并单位与成立法人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two lumps of dough folded until the seam cannot be found.
core.cn: 核心意象：两块面团折叠到找不出接缝。

branches.en: PRODUCT LINE: a feature is built into the whole.
branches.cn: 产品线：某项功能被造进整体里。

branches.en: IDEA LINE: advice is kneaded into a plan.
branches.cn: 想法线：建议被揉进计划里。

branches.en: UNION LINE: two units are given one body.
branches.cn: 联合线：两个单位拥有同一个身体。

branches.en: LAW LINE: a business receives a legal body.
branches.cn: 法律线：企业获得法律意义上的身体。

branches.en: CRAFT LINE: the maker hides the joins but keeps the strength.
branches.cn: 手艺线：制作者把接缝藏起来，却保留强度。

intro.en: A Latin prefix for inside, a root meaning body, and a verb ending for making.
intro.cn: 一个表「在内」的拉丁前缀、一个意为「身体」的词根，以及表示「使之成为」的动词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin corpus, body, with in and -are, gave incorporare, to make into one body.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 corpus「身体」结合 in 与 -are，构成 incorporare「使成一体」。

items.example: a body and a corpse share one root
items.exampleCN: 身体与尸体同出一个词根

definition_en: to become larger in amount, number or degree, or to make something larger
core_image: 温度计里的红线一节一节往上爬
scene: 入冬后，早高峰的公交总是一年比一年挤。Ticket prices increase every January.
sceneCN: 这里 increase 是「上涨」（第 1 个义项：数量或程度变大）；句意是票价每年一月上涨。

pos.zh: 动词：增加；增长；增大
名词：增加；增长；增量

derivatives.zh: 义为「不断增加的」，如 increasing pressure
义为「日益、越来越」
义为「减少」，与 increase 反义同构

senses.title: To grow in amount or number
senses.titleCN: 增加：数量或数目变大
senses.definition: to become larger in size, amount or number
senses.definitionCN: 在规模、数量或数目上变大
senses.example: Ticket prices increase every January.
senses.exampleCN: 票价每年一月上涨。
senses.why: The Latin crescere means to grow, and in-crescere is to grow into something bigger.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 crescere 意为「生长」，in-crescere 就是长成更大的样子。

senses.title: To make something larger
senses.titleCN: 使增加：把某物提高
senses.definition: to raise a figure, level or output by one's own action
senses.definitionCN: 通过自身行动把数字、水平或产量提高
senses.example: The factory plans to increase output by a fifth.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂计划把产量提高五分之一。
senses.why: The verb is both intransitive and transitive, because growth can happen or be caused.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词既可不及物也可及物，因为增长既可以自己发生，也可以被促成。

senses.title: To become stronger in degree
senses.titleCN: 增强：程度变深
senses.definition: to become greater in intensity, such as pain, pressure or risk
senses.definitionCN: 在强度上变大，如疼痛、压力或风险
senses.example: Noise from the road increases at night.
senses.exampleCN: 夜里路上的噪音会增大。
senses.why: Not everything that grows is countable: pressure and pain also swell.
senses.whyCN: 并非所有增长都能计数：压力与疼痛也会膨胀。

senses.title: The noun, a rise in amount
senses.titleCN: 增幅：名词，指上升的量
senses.definition: a rise in amount, price or level, often measured against an earlier figure
senses.definitionCN: 数量、价格或水平的上升，常与先前数字相较
senses.example: There was a sharp increase in rainfall last summer.
senses.exampleCN: 去年夏天降雨量急剧增加。
senses.why: English turns the verb into a noun without changing its shape, only its stress.
senses.whyCN: 英语把这个动词直接变成名词，形状不变，只挪动重音。

senses.title: In phrases, on the rise
senses.titleCN: 在增加中：用于固定短语
senses.definition: used in the phrase on the increase to mean becoming more common
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 on the increase，表示日益增多
senses.example: Cheating in exams is on the increase.
senses.exampleCN: 考试作弊的现象在增多。
senses.why: The noun settles into a fixed idiom that reports a trend rather than a single event.
senses.whyCN: 名词固定成一个习语，用来报道趋势而不是单次事件。

intro.en: Increase comes from Latin increscere, to grow in, from in and crescere, to grow.
intro.cn: increase 来自拉丁语 increscere「在里面生长」，由 in 与 crescere「生长」构成。

items.en: Crescere meant to grow, as plants and children do.
items.cn: crescere 意为「生长」，如植物与孩子长大。

items.en: French encreistre carried the word into everyday use about crops and wealth.
items.cn: 法语 encreistre 把这个词带入关于收成与财富的日常用法。

items.en: English borrowed it as encresen, first as a verb only.
items.cn: 英语借作 encresen，最初只有动词用法。

items.en: The noun appeared in the fourteenth century with a different stress pattern.
items.cn: 名词在十四世纪出现，并带有不同的重音模式。

items.en: Statistics and economics made both forms central to reporting trends.
items.cn: 统计学与经济学让两种形式都成为报道趋势的核心词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -crease growth root; the near-meaning group holds verbs of going up.
note.cn: 形近组共用表示「生长」的 -crease 词根；近义组收表示「上升」的动词。

entries.definition: To become smaller in amount.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「减少」，与 increase 反义同根。

entries.definition: More and more over time.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「日益、越来越」。

entries.definition: A small regular addition.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「增量、增额」。

entries.definition: To go up, often used of prices and levels.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「上升、上涨」。

entries.definition: To become larger over time.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「生长、增长」，更偏自然过程。

entries.definition: To become larger in size or scope.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「扩大」，偏规模与体积。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the growing root, the thermometer and the stress shift between verb and noun.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借「生长」词根、温度计和动名之间的重音移动。

normal.en: In plus crease: growth happens inside the thing itself, not bolted on from outside.
normal.cn: in 加 crease：生长发生在事物内部，不是从外面钉上去的。

normal.en: Decrease is the same root with de-, so the pair is a rising and a falling line.
normal.cn: decrease 同根但用 de-，这一对就是上升线与下降线。

normal.en: Stress moves: inCREASE as a verb, INcrease as a noun, a common English habit.
normal.cn: 重音会挪：动词读 inCREASE，名词读 INcrease，这是英语常见习惯。

normal.en: On the increase means the trend line is still climbing.
normal.cn: on the increase 意思是趋势线还在往上爬。

normal.en: Increase by is the size of the jump, while increase to is where it lands.
normal.cn: increase by 指跳了多少，increase to 指跳到哪里。

abstract.en: Growth is the only change that keeps its own shape as it changes.
abstract.cn: 增长是唯一在变化中仍保持自身形状的变化。

abstract.en: A number that increases never explains itself; the reason always sits outside the chart.
abstract.cn: 一个增加的数字从不解释自己，原因永远在图表之外。

abstract.en: What increases without limit is usually the thing nobody is measuring.
abstract.cn: 无限增长的，往往正是没人去计量的那样东西。

examples.en: The number of students increased by nearly a hundred.
examples.cn: 学生人数增加了将近一百。

examples.en: Exercise can increase your energy level.
examples.cn: 锻炼能提高你的精力水平。

examples.en: The company reported an increase in sales.
examples.cn: 公司报告销售额有所增长。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因快死」——人数因疫情快速变化，增长的忧愁里带着个快字。

root: 拉丁语 in（在内）+ crescere（生长）→ increscere（长起来）；同根词有 decrease、increment、crescent、concrete。

sensesIntro.en: Increase says that something grows inside its own frame, and the word then extends from counts to intensity and finally to a noun for a trend.
sensesIntro.cn: increase 说的是某物在自己的框架里长起来，于是从数量扩展到强度，最后成为表示趋势的名词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the red line in a thermometer climbing notch by notch.
core.cn: 核心意象：温度计里的红线一格一格往上爬。

branches.en: COUNT LINE: numbers of things get larger.
branches.cn: 数量线：事物的数目变大。

branches.en: ACTION LINE: someone raises output on purpose.
branches.cn: 行动线：有人有意提高产量。

branches.en: DEGREE LINE: pressure and noise swell.
branches.cn: 程度线：压力与噪音一起膨胀。

branches.en: NOUN LINE: the rise itself becomes a thing to report.
branches.cn: 名词线：上升本身变成一个可报道的对象。

branches.en: IDIOM LINE: a fixed phrase describes a trend.
branches.cn: 习语线：固定说法描述一种趋势。

intro.en: A Latin prefix for inward growth and a root for growing, plus a large family of -crease words.
intro.cn: 一个表「向内生长」的拉丁前缀与表示「生长」的词根，加上一族 -crease 词。

latinIntro.en: Latin crescere, to grow, gave increscere, to grow on, and English took both halves.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 crescere「生长」生出 increscere「长起来」，英语把两部分都借了过来。

items.example: the root of increase and decrease
items.exampleCN: increase 与 decrease 的共同词根

definition_en: more and more as time passes
core_image: 台阶一级一级往上，每一级都比前一级更高
scene: 这几年，很多事都在悄悄变得更难。Students are increasingly worried about finding work.
sceneCN: 这里 increasingly 是「越来越」（第 1 个义项：随时间推移程度加深）；句意是学生们越来越担心找工作。

pos.zh: 副词：日益；愈加；日趋

forms.label: 无变化（副词无词形变化）

derivatives.zh: 义为「增加、增长」，是本词的动词基础
义为「不断增加的」
义为「越来越少地」，与本词相反

senses.title: More and more over time
senses.titleCN: 越来越：随时间不断加深
senses.definition: used with an adjective to show that a quality grows over time
senses.definitionCN: 与形容词连用，表示某种性质随时间不断增强
senses.example: Students are increasingly worried about finding work.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们越来越担心找工作。
senses.why: The -ly adverb keeps the growth of increase and turns it into a rising curve beside another word.
senses.whyCN: -ly 副词保留了 increase 的「生长」义，并把它变成紧挨另一个词的上升曲线。

senses.title: Used of a trend, not a single step
senses.titleCN: 日益：用于趋势而非单次变化
senses.definition: describing a gradual shift observed across a period rather than one event
senses.definitionCN: 描述在一段时期内观察到的渐变，而非单次事件
senses.example: The city has become increasingly quiet at night.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市夜里变得日益安静。
senses.why: A single change is described by increase, but only a long drift earns the adverb.
senses.whyCN: 单次变化用 increase 就够，只有长期漂移才配得上这个副词。

senses.title: Used for growing degree in an argument
senses.titleCN: 愈加：在论述中强调程度递进
senses.definition: used to stress that one statement matters more as the argument goes on
senses.definitionCN: 用于强调随着论述推进，某一说法愈发重要
senses.example: It is increasingly hard to defend that view.
senses.exampleCN: 那种观点越来越难以辩护。
senses.why: Writers borrow the adverb to let a claim sound like an approaching tide.
senses.whyCN: 写作者借用这个副词，让论断听起来像渐渐逼近的潮水。

intro.en: Increasingly is increase with the adjective ending -ing and the adverb ending -ly added in Modern English.
intro.cn: increasingly 是 increase 加形容词词尾 -ing、再加副词词尾 -ly 构成的现代英语派生词。

items.en: Crescere, to grow, gave increscere, to grow into.
items.cn: crescere「生长」生出 increscere「长起来」。

items.en: The verb encresen entered English from French.
items.cn: 动词 encresen 由法语进入英语。

items.en: The present participle increasing began to work as an adjective.
items.cn: 现在分词 increasing 开始充当形容词。

items.en: Adding -ly produced the adverb in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 加 -ly 后，这个副词在十九世纪成型。

items.en: Modern journalism made it a standard word for trends.
items.cn: 现代新闻写作让它成为描述趋势的常用词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the increase stem; the near-meaning group holds adverbs of worsening degree.
note.cn: 形近组共用 increase 词干；近义组收表示程度加深的副词。

entries.definition: To become larger in amount.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「增加」，是本词的基础。

entries.definition: Becoming larger over time.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不断增加的」。

entries.definition: Less and less as time passes.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「越来越少地」。

entries.definition: Slowly over a period of time.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「逐渐地」，重在慢。

entries.definition: In stages, step by step.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「逐步地」，重在分阶段。

entries.definition: Used with comparatives to mean always more.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，与比较级连用表示「越来越」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the staircase image, the -ly adverb slot and the trend word of news writing.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借台阶意象、-ly 副词位置与新闻里的趋势表达。

normal.en: Increase plus -ing plus -ly: a growth that never finishes and only describes another word.
normal.cn: increase 加 -ing 再加 -ly：一个永不结束的生长，只用来修饰别的词。

normal.en: It almost never stands alone; it leans on an adjective such as difficult or important.
normal.cn: 它几乎不单独站立，总倚着一个形容词，如 difficult 或 important。

normal.en: If one step is a jump, this word describes the whole staircase.
normal.cn: 如果一步是跳跃，这个词描述的是整座楼梯。

normal.en: Decrease the first letter and the direction of the staircase reverses.
normal.cn: 把首字母换一换，楼梯的方向就反过来。

normal.en: News headlines love it because it reports a drift without naming a cause.
normal.cn: 新闻标题偏爱它，因为它只报道漂移，不指明原因。

abstract.en: Slow change is the only kind the naked eye cannot catch while it happens.
abstract.cn: 缓慢的变化是唯一在发生当下无法被肉眼捕捉的变化。

abstract.en: To say increasingly is to admit that no single instant can show the shift.
abstract.cn: 说「越来越」，等于承认没有任何一个瞬间能显示这次转变。

abstract.en: The adverb measures direction, while the reader still has to guess the speed.
abstract.cn: 这个副词只测方向，速度仍要读者自己去猜。

examples.en: Housing in the city is becoming increasingly expensive.
examples.cn: 这座城市的住房越来越贵。

examples.en: People increasingly work from home.
examples.cn: 人们越来越多地在家办公。

examples.en: It is increasingly rare to see a public phone.
examples.cn: 公共电话越来越少见。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「印快格林里」——印得越来越快，纸一摞摞往格林里堆。

root: 拉丁语 crescere（生长）→ increscere → increase；加 -ing、-ly 构成 increasingly。

sensesIntro.en: Increasingly takes the growth inside increase and turns it into an adverb that always leans on another word and reports a long drift.
sensesIntro.cn: increasingly 把 increase 里的生长变成副词，它总要倚着另一个词，报道的是一段漫长的漂移。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a staircase whose every step is higher than the last.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座每级都比上一级更高的楼梯。

branches.en: QUALITY LINE: a quality deepens beside an adjective.
branches.cn: 性质线：某种性质在形容词旁边加深。

branches.en: PERIOD LINE: the change is spread across years.
branches.cn: 时段线：变化摊展在数年之间。

branches.en: ARGUMENT LINE: a claim gains force as the case goes on.
branches.cn: 论述线：说法随着论证推进而更有力。

branches.en: RHYTHM LINE: the word marks direction, not speed.
branches.cn: 节奏线：这个词标方向，不标速度。

branches.en: TONE LINE: writers use it to sound calm about bad news.
branches.cn: 语气线：写作者用它把坏消息说得平静。

intro.en: A growth root with a participial ending and an adverb ending stacked on top.
intro.cn: 一个「生长」词根上依次叠加分词词尾与副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin crescere, to grow, gave increscere; English added -ing and -ly.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 crescere「生长」生出 increscere，英语再加上 -ing 与 -ly。

definition_zh: 难以置信的；惊人的；极好的
definition_en: too strange or extreme to be believed, or extremely good
core_image: 听见一句话，眉毛先跳起来，嘴还没张开
scene: 朋友说自己一夜游过海峡，你第一反应是不信。It sounds incredible, but she finished the race in under three hours.
sceneCN: 这里 incredible 是「难以置信的」（第 1 个义项：难以相信）；句意是听起来难以置信，但她不到三小时就跑完了全程。

pos.zh: 形容词：难以置信的；惊人的；极好的

derivatives.zh: 义为「难以置信地；极其」，由本词加 -ly 构成
义为「可信的」，去掉 in- 即成肯定形式
义为「信任、信用」，与本词同根
义为「可信度」

senses.title: Too strange to believe
senses.titleCN: 难以置信：奇怪到无法相信
senses.definition: so unusual or extreme that it is hard to believe
senses.definitionCN: 极其反常或极端，令人难信
senses.example: It sounds incredible, but she finished the race in under three hours.
senses.exampleCN: 听起来难以置信，但她不到三小时就跑完了全程。
senses.why: The Latin credere means to believe, and the negative prefix in- says no: not to be believed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 credere 意为「相信」，否定前缀 in- 说「不」：不可被相信。

senses.title: Extremely large or great
senses.titleCN: 惊人的：规模或程度极大
senses.definition: so great in size or amount that it surprises the mind
senses.definitionCN: 在规模或数量上大到让人吃惊
senses.example: The team worked at incredible speed.
senses.exampleCN: 这个团队以惊人的速度工作。
senses.why: When a number passes belief, the same word measures size rather than truth.
senses.whyCN: 当一个数字超出相信的范围，同一个词就转而衡量大小而非真伪。

senses.title: Extremely good, in speech
senses.titleCN: 极好的：口语中的赞叹
senses.definition: used informally to praise something as wonderful
senses.definitionCN: 口语中用来称赞某物好极了
senses.example: The view from the top was incredible.
senses.exampleCN: 山顶的景色美极了。
senses.why: Praise borrows the same exclamation: what is beyond belief is also beyond the ordinary.
senses.whyCN: 赞叹借用了同一句惊叹：超出相信的，也超出寻常。

senses.title: Hard to accept, used of behaviour
senses.titleCN: 难以接受：形容行为过分
senses.definition: used of behaviour that seems shockingly unfair or careless
senses.definitionCN: 形容行为不公或粗心到令人震惊
senses.example: It is incredible that they left the door unlocked.
senses.exampleCN: 他们竟没锁门，真让人难以接受。
senses.why: The negative prefix carries moral weight too: such conduct should not be believed of anyone.
senses.whyCN: 否定前缀也带道德分量：这种行为不该被相信会出自任何人。

intro.en: Incredible comes from Latin incredibilis, from in-, not, and credere, to believe.
intro.cn: incredible 来自拉丁语 incredibilis，由 in-（不）与 credere（相信）构成。

items.en: Credere meant to trust or to entrust, the source of credit and creed.
items.cn: credere 意为「信任、托付」，是 credit 与 creed 的来源。

items.en: Incredibilis named what could not be believed, often of marvels.
items.cn: incredibilis 指令人无法相信之事，常用于奇闻。

items.en: English borrowed it through French for tales that defied belief.
items.cn: 英语经由法语借入，用于不合常理的故事。

items.en: The sense widened from untrue to merely astonishing.
items.cn: 词义从「不真」扩展到「仅仅令人吃惊」。

items.en: Spoken English added the sense of extremely good.
items.cn: 英语口语又添上「极好」的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cred- believe root; the near-meaning group holds words of surprise.
note.cn: 形近组共用表示「相信」的 cred- 词根；近义组收表示「惊异」的词。

entries.definition: Able to be believed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可信的」，与本词只差一个 in-。

entries.definition: In a way that is hard to believe.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「难以置信地」。

entries.definition: Trust that allows buying now and paying later.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「信用、赊账」，同根。

entries.definition: Impossible or very hard to believe.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「难以置信的」，更口语。

entries.definition: So surprising that one is stunned.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「惊人的」，重在看后发懵。

entries.definition: Very surprising and impressive.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人惊叹的」，偏褒义。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the believe root, the cred-credible pair and the everyday exclamation.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借「相信」词根、cred/credible 对照与日常惊叹。

normal.en: Credit and creed both hold cred, believe, so incredible means simply not-credible.
normal.cn: credit 与 creed 里都含 cred「相信」，所以 incredible 就是「不可信的」。

normal.en: Take away in- and credible remains, which makes the pair the easiest negative in English.
normal.cn: 去掉 in- 剩下 credible，这一对是英语里最好记的否定搭配。

normal.en: When a story is incredible, the eyebrow moves before the mouth does.
normal.cn: 故事令人难以置信时，眉毛先于嘴巴做出反应。

normal.en: The same word praises dinner and prices, because both can pass belief.
normal.cn: 同一个词既夸晚饭也形容价格，因为两者都可能超出想象。

normal.en: An incredible amount is not a claim about truth but about the size of the pile.
normal.cn: an incredible amount 不是在说真假，而是在说那一堆有多大。

abstract.en: Belief is the most portable currency: it buys claims, goods and people alike.
abstract.cn: 相信是最通用的货币：它能买到说法、货物与人。

abstract.en: What is incredible is not always false, only unwitnessed.
abstract.cn: 难以置信的不一定假，只是尚未被亲眼看见。

abstract.en: Every wonder starts as a sentence the listener refuses to accept.
abstract.cn: 每一件奇事起初都是一句听者拒绝接受的话。

examples.en: They made an incredible amount of noise.
examples.cn: 他们弄出了惊人的动静。

examples.en: Her recovery was incredible to the doctors.
examples.cn: 她的康复让医生们难以置信。

examples.en: What an incredible meal that was!
examples.cn: 那顿饭真是好极了！

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因克瑞德」——因一张信用卡被克扣，账单令人难以置信。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ credere（相信）→ incredibilis；同根词有 credible、credit、credibility、creed、credential。

sensesIntro.en: Incredible begins as the simple denial of belief, then measures size, and finally becomes a spoken word of praise.
sensesIntro.cn: incredible 起初只是对「相信」的简单否定，后来用来衡量大小，最后变成口语中的赞美。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: eyebrows jumping before the mouth can answer.
core.cn: 核心意象：嘴巴还没开口，眉毛先跳了起来。

branches.en: TRUTH LINE: the tale resists belief.
branches.cn: 真伪线：故事抗拒被相信。

branches.en: SIZE LINE: a quantity passes the limit of imagination.
branches.cn: 大小线：数量越过想象的边界。

branches.en: PRAISE LINE: everyday speech turns it into a compliment.
branches.cn: 赞美线：日常口语把它变成褒义词。

branches.en: JUDGEMENT LINE: conduct is judged too unlikely to accept.
branches.cn: 评判线：某种行为被判为难以接受。

branches.en: TONE LINE: one adjective can be a doubt or a compliment.
branches.cn: 语气线：同一个形容词既可是疑问也可是称赞。

intro.en: A negative prefix on a root meaning believe, with an adjective ending that makes it describable.
intro.cn: 一个否定前缀加意为「相信」的词根，再接形容词词尾，使之可用来形容事物。

latinIntro.en: Latin in-, not, plus credere, to believe, plus -ibilis, able to be, gave incredibilis.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 in-「不」加 credere「相信」加 -ibilis「可……的」，构成 incredibilis。

items.example: the root of credible and credit
items.exampleCN: credible 与 credit 的词根

definition_en: used to emphasize that something is true, or to add a stronger statement
core_image: 点了点头，又把手按在桌上补一句「真的」
scene: 别人怀疑你的说法时，你会加重语气再确认一次。It was indeed the coldest night of the year.
sceneCN: 这里 indeed 是「确实」（第 1 个义项：强调所说的为真）；句意是那确实是全年最冷的一夜。

pos.zh: 副词：确实；的确；实际上

forms.label: 无变化（副词无词形变化）

derivatives.zh: 义为「行为、事迹」，是本词的后半部分
义为「超过」，与 indeed 的 -ceed 部分形近，注意区分

senses.title: Emphasizing that something is true
senses.titleCN: 确实：强调某事为真
senses.definition: used to make a statement stronger or to confirm it
senses.definitionCN: 用来加强或确认某个说法
senses.example: It was indeed the coldest night of the year.
senses.exampleCN: 那确实是全年最冷的一夜。
senses.why: The word is literally in deed, in the fact of the matter, so it points at reality itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个词字面上就是「在事实中」，所以它直接指向现实本身。

senses.title: Adding a stronger point
senses.titleCN: 而且：补上更进一步的说法
senses.definition: used to introduce a further and stronger piece of information
senses.definitionCN: 用来引出更进一步、更有力的信息
senses.example: He is a good teacher, indeed a great one.
senses.exampleCN: 他是位好老师，而且是一位了不起的老师。
senses.why: Confirming one fact opens the door to a bigger one, so the word also links escalations.
senses.whyCN: 确认一件事就打开了更大的门，因此这个词也用来连接递进。

senses.title: After very or an adjective, as intensifier
senses.titleCN: 非常：放在形容词后加强程度
senses.definition: placed after very and an adjective to strengthen the description
senses.definitionCN: 放在 very 加形容词之后，加强描述
senses.example: She was very tired indeed.
senses.exampleCN: 她确实非常累。
senses.why: At the end of a phrase the word becomes a stamp of emphasis, almost a nod.
senses.whyCN: 放在短语末尾时，它变成一枚强调的印章，几乎就是一个点头。

senses.title: Showing surprise or interest
senses.titleCN: 真的吗：表示惊讶或兴趣
senses.definition: used in speech to show mild surprise or to invite more talk
senses.definitionCN: 口语中表示轻微的惊讶，或邀请对方继续讲
senses.example: Indeed? I had not heard about that.
senses.exampleCN: 真的吗？我还没听说过这事。
senses.why: The same confirmation becomes a question when the voice rises, a common speech habit.
senses.whyCN: 同一个确认词在语调上扬时就成了疑问，这是常见的口语习惯。

intro.en: Indeed is a Middle English compound of in and deed, meaning in fact or in reality.
intro.cn: indeed 是中古英语合成词，由 in 与 deed「行为、事实」构成，意为「在事实上」。

items.en: Dæd meant a deed or an act, the thing actually done.
items.cn: dæd 意为行为或事迹，即实际做出的事。

items.en: In dede was a phrase meaning in fact, written as one word later.
items.cn: in dede 是「事实上」的短语，后来写成一个词。

items.en: The word became a common way to confirm an assertion.
items.cn: 这个词成为确认论断的常用手段。

items.en: It also took the linking sense of a further, stronger point.
items.cn: 它也承担起引出更进一步说法的连接作用。

items.en: Spoken use added the surprised question, spoken with a rising tone.
items.cn: 口语用法又添上带上扬语调的惊讶疑问。

note.en: The look-alike group shares short in- words; the near-meaning group holds adverbs of emphasis and confirmation.
note.cn: 形近组收以 in- 开头的短词；近义组收表示强调与确认的副词。

entries.definition: An action that is done.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「行为、事迹」。

entries.definition: To start a line further from the margin.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「缩进」，与 indeed 形近。

entries.definition: An alphabetical list at the end of a book.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「索引」，与 indeed 形近。

entries.definition: Without doubt.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「当然、肯定」。

entries.definition: In fact, used to correct a belief.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「实际上」，常用于纠正看法。

entries.definition: In a genuine way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「真正地」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the literal in-deed reading, the sentence-final stamp and the rising question.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借字面的 in-deed 结构、句末盖章与上扬疑问。

normal.en: In plus deed is in the deed, in what was actually done, so indeed means in fact.
normal.cn: in 加 deed 就是「在行为中」，即在真正做过的事里，所以意为「事实上」。

normal.en: A friend indeed is a friend in deeds, not merely in words, a proverb that explains the word.
normal.cn: a friend indeed 是「在行动上」的朋友而非只在嘴上，这句谚语正好解释这个词。

normal.en: Very tired indeed puts the nod at the end of the sentence.
normal.cn: very tired indeed 把那个点头放在句末。

normal.en: He is good, indeed great: the second statement is a step higher than the first.
normal.cn: He is good, indeed great：后一句比前一句又高了一级。

normal.en: Say it with a rising voice and the same word becomes really?
normal.cn: 把语调扬起来，同一个词就变成了「真的吗？」

abstract.en: Indeed is the shortest form of evidence: it points at the deed instead of describing it.
abstract.cn: indeed 是最短的证据形式：它指向行为，而不描述行为。

abstract.en: To confirm is a social act, so the word always assumes someone who doubted.
abstract.cn: 确认是一种社交行为，所以这个词总预设了一个曾怀疑的人。

abstract.en: A sentence ending in indeed leaves no room for the listener to disagree quietly.
abstract.cn: 以 indeed 收尾的句子，不留给听者悄悄反对的余地。

examples.en: Thank you very much indeed.
examples.cn: 真是非常感谢。

examples.en: The task was hard, indeed almost impossible.
examples.cn: 这项任务很难，几乎不可能完成。

examples.en: Indeed, the plan worked better than we hoped.
examples.cn: 的确，这计划比我们预想的更成功。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「印底的」——印在纸底的那行字，的确是证据。

root: 中古英语 in（在）+ deed（行为、事实）→ in dede（事实上）→ indeed。

sensesIntro.en: Indeed starts as a pointer to a deed, becomes a stamp of truth, then a step up in argument, a sentence-final intensifier and finally a surprised question.
sensesIntro.cn: indeed 起初指向「行为」，后来成为真实的印章，再变成论述中的递进、句末的加强，最后成了惊讶的疑问。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a nod of the head, then a hand pressed flat on the table.
core.cn: 核心意象：先点头，再把手平按在桌上。

branches.en: TRUTH LINE: the word points at what really happened.
branches.cn: 真实线：这个词指向真正发生的事。

branches.en: ESCALATION LINE: the next claim goes one step further.
branches.cn: 递进线：下一个说法再进一层。

branches.en: STAMP LINE: placed after an adjective, it seals the description.
branches.cn: 盖章线：放在形容词后，为描述封口。

branches.en: SPEECH LINE: a rising tone turns it into a question.
branches.cn: 口语线：上扬的语调把它变成疑问。

branches.en: RHETORIC LINE: confirming first makes a bigger claim easier to accept.
branches.cn: 修辞线：先确认小事，大话更容易被接受。

intro.en: A preposition fused with an Old English noun of action, plus a short family of -deed words.
intro.cn: 一个介词与一个古英语行为名词熔成一词，外加一族简短的 -deed 词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin equivalent structure is in facto, in the fact, which also gives English fact and feat.
latinIntro.cn: 对应的拉丁结构是 in facto「在事实中」，英语由此得到 fact 与 feat。

items.example: He said so, and indeed so it was.
items.exampleCN: 他这么说，事实也确是如此。

items.meaning: in action, not only in words
items.meaningCN: 在行动上，而不只在口头上
items.example: help in deed as well as in word

items.meaning: a document that transfers a gift

definition_en: freedom from control by another person, group or country
core_image: 一只鸟第一次不再靠着巢沿，自己张开翅膀
scene: 搬出父母家，才真正懂得独立是什么味道。Living alone taught her independence.
sceneCN: 这里 independence 是「独立」（第 1 个义项：不依赖他人）；句意是独自生活教会了她独立。

pos.zh: 名词：独立；自主；不受支配

derivatives.zh: 义为「独立的」，是本词的形容词形式
义为「独立地」
义为「依赖」，去掉 in- 即成相反名词
义为「依靠」，与本词同根

senses.title: Freedom from another's control
senses.titleCN: 独立：不受他人支配
senses.definition: the state of not being controlled or supported by another person
senses.definitionCN: 不被他人控制或供养的状态
senses.example: Living alone taught her independence.
senses.exampleCN: 独自生活教会了她独立。
senses.why: The word is in- not plus depend, to hang from, so independence means not hanging from anyone.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 in-（不）加 depend（悬靠），所以独立就是不再挂在任何人身上。

senses.title: A nation's self-rule
senses.titleCN: 国家独立：自主治理
senses.definition: the freedom of a country to govern itself
senses.definitionCN: 一个国家自行治理的自由
senses.example: The country declared independence in nineteen sixty.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家在一九六零年宣布独立。
senses.why: Politics simply lifts the personal image to the scale of a whole people.
senses.whyCN: 政治只是把个人的意象放大到整个民族的尺度。

senses.title: Money that needs no patron
senses.titleCN: 经济独立：不靠他人供养
senses.definition: having enough income to live without help from others
senses.definitionCN: 拥有足够收入、无需他人帮助也能生活
senses.example: A part-time job gave him financial independence.
senses.exampleCN: 一份兼职让他经济上独立了。
senses.why: Money is the modern rope that ties people to each other, so cutting it makes them independent.
senses.whyCN: 金钱是现代社会把人系在一起的绳索，剪断它人便独立了。

senses.title: Separateness in thought or method
senses.titleCN: 独立性：思想或方法上自成一体
senses.definition: the quality of forming one's own judgement rather than copying others
senses.definitionCN: 形成自己的判断而非照搬他人的品质
senses.example: Her research shows real independence of mind.
senses.exampleCN: 她的研究显示出真正的思想独立性。
senses.why: Beyond bodies and borders, the word describes a mind that does not lean on another.
senses.whyCN: 除了身体与国界，这个词还形容一颗不倚靠别人的心。

intro.en: Independence is in-, not, plus dependence, from Latin dependere, to hang from.
intro.cn: independence 是 in-（不）加 dependence，后者源自拉丁语 dependere「悬挂于」。

items.en: Dependere meant to hang down from something, from de- and pendere.
items.cn: dependere 意为「从某物上垂挂」，由 de- 与 pendere 构成。

items.en: Depend entered English with the sense of being supported by another.
items.cn: depend 进入英语时带有「依靠他人支撑」之义。

items.en: Independence appeared in the seventeenth century for freedom from control.
items.cn: independence 在十七世纪出现，表示不受控制。

items.en: Political use spread after the American Declaration in seventeen seventy-six.
items.cn: 一七七六年美国《独立宣言》之后，政治用法广泛流传。

items.en: Personal and financial senses grew in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.
items.cn: 个人与经济层面的义项在十九、二十世纪发展起来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the pend- hang root; the near-meaning group holds words of freedom and self-rule.
note.cn: 形近组共用表示「悬挂」的 pend- 词根；近义组收表示自由与自决的词。

entries.definition: Free from control by others.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「独立的」。

entries.definition: The state of needing help.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「依赖」。

entries.definition: A person who depends on another by custom or law.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「受抚养者」。

entries.definition: The power to act as one wishes.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「自由」。

entries.definition: The right of a group to govern itself.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「自治」，多为术语。

entries.definition: Reliance on one's own powers.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「自力更生」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the hanging root, the bird leaving the nest and the declaration of independence.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借「悬挂」词根、离巢的鸟与独立宣言。

normal.en: Depend is to hang down from someone, so independence is the moment the hook is removed.
normal.cn: depend 是挂在某人身上，那么独立就是钩子被取下的时刻。

normal.en: The verb is depend, the adjective independent, the noun independence: only the ending changes.
normal.cn: 动词 depend、形容词 independent、名词 independence，只换词尾。

normal.en: Dependence and independence face each other with one small in- between.
normal.cn: dependence 与 independence 只隔一个小小的 in-。

normal.en: A baby bird at the nest edge is the best picture: first it flaps, then it lets go.
normal.cn: 巢沿的雏鸟是最好的画面：先扇翅，再放手。

normal.en: Independence Day celebrates a document that ended a hanging rope across the ocean.
normal.cn: 独立日纪念的是一纸文书，它剪断了横跨大洋的那根绳。

abstract.en: Independence is measured not by who you leave but by who no longer has to carry you.
abstract.cn: 独立不看离开了谁，而看谁不必再把你背着。

abstract.en: True autonomy keeps the link but gives it a looser knot.
abstract.cn: 真正的自主保留联结，只把绳结放松。

abstract.en: A mind that never leans will never know what it believes.
abstract.cn: 从不倚靠的心，也不会知道自己相信什么。

examples.en: She values her independence more than a big salary.
examples.cn: 比起高薪，她更看重自己的独立。

examples.en: The colony fought for independence.
examples.cn: 这块殖民地曾为独立而战。

examples.en: Learning to cook is a first step towards independence.
examples.cn: 学会做饭是迈向独立的第一步。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「印地盆等次」——自己占地印盆，不必等别人赏赐，便是独立。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ dependere（悬挂于，来自 de- + pendere「悬挂」）→ independence；同根词有 depend、dependent、pendant、suspend。

sensesIntro.en: Independence begins as the removal of an outer hook, then scales to a country's self-rule, to money without a patron, and to a mind that judges for itself.
sensesIntro.cn: independence 起初是不再挂在钩上，而后扩展到国家的自主、无须供养人的财富，以及自做判断的心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a young bird letting go of the nest edge on its first flight.
core.cn: 核心意象：雏鸟第一次放手离巢。

branches.en: PERSONAL LINE: no one else gives the orders.
branches.cn: 个人线：不再由他人发号令。

branches.en: POLITICAL LINE: a country governs itself.
branches.cn: 政治线：国家自行治理。

branches.en: MONEY LINE: income arrives without a patron.
branches.cn: 金钱线：收入不必来自恩主。

branches.en: MIND LINE: judgement is formed alone.
branches.cn: 思想线：判断由自己形成。

branches.en: GROWTH LINE: independence is usually won step by step.
branches.cn: 成长线：独立往往一步一步赢来。

intro.en: A negative prefix, a prefix meaning down, a root meaning hang and a noun ending.
intro.cn: 一个否定前缀、一个表示「向下」的前缀、一个意为「悬挂」的词根，以及一个名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin pendere, to hang, with de-, down, gave dependere, to hang from; in- then denies it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pendere「悬挂」加 de-「向下」成为 dependere「悬于」，再加 in- 加以否定。

items.example: the root of suspend and pendant
items.exampleCN: suspend 与 pendant 的词根

state of not hanging from others
